defects: A literal-only exception initializer escaped the existing marker-exception review.
A conditional literal SQL append prevented recovery of an authored cross-model join.
A single raw ID and its stable same-file abstract implementation escaped nominal-ID review.
A final awaited lookup inside a resource context was split from its outer None guard.
Connection execution and prepared loop bodies escaped the narrow cursor executemany advisory.
Repeated cursor creation and comparison-time UUID reparsing had no owning review rule.
Existing frontend comment hygiene permitted prose and executable directives despite the requested blanket policy.
admission.safety: Semantic changes to result contracts, queries, normalization and resource scopes remain manual. No new automatic fix removes validation, changes transactions, or deletes behavioral/legal comments.

validation.builtin_source_preflight: No blocking diagnostics; inherited warning findings were retained separately.
validation.native_lint_and_typing: Passed before documentation comment migration; canonical verification covers final source.
validation.introduced_match_inspection: Every introduced match was reviewed. Existing Python marker warnings retained their locations and received updated guidance.
validation.same_input_repeatability: Every batch compared all four repeated diagnostic sets for equality.
validation.precedence: SARJ518 owns the overlapping batchable-write diagnostic when selected; SARJ560 remains effective when selected alone. Recognized frontend tests are owned by no-test-comments.
validation.resource_guard_autofix: A cross-context walrus candidate is warning-only and fix_source preserves the original bytes.
validation.self_adoption: Sixteen maintained docs-app comments were removed; private helpers were reordered and an existing build-provenance environment exception was moved into configuration.

isolation.ordering: Alternating baseline/candidate order; fresh process for every corpus and batch.
isolation.combined_sample: Thirty tracked public source files selected by ascending SHA-256 of relative path. This panel overlaps the main corpora and is reported separately, not as independent coverage.
isolation.pins: Verified before and after each isolated panel without repinning. Private identities, paths and digests are omitted.

performance_method: Cold is the first analysis in a fresh batch process after imports; warm is the median of the next three analyses. Each panel sums its batch times per round, then takes the median of three rounds. No OS/shared caches were cleared. Shared-VM timings varied; this is a compatibility measurement, not an optimization claim.
limitations: Exception expectedness and imported framework contracts still need review.
Dynamic SQL rewrites, wildcard/dynamic namespaces and unsupported relation ownership abstain.
Unknown, imported, decorated, mutated and multiple-inheritance ID contracts remain conservative.
While retry/stream loops, interprocedural SQL execution and intentionally chunked executemany loops remain outside the new loop warning.
Multiple cursors and cross-context optional guards can be intentional; no automatic rewrite changes their contracts.
Frontend ownership uses syntax and nearest package metadata; unsupported frameworks can opt in with allFiles on both comment rules.
The requested examples are pinned source snapshots; a full external consumer workspace/type graph was not reconstructed.
reproduce: Run the focused native tests for every changed rule and its neighboring owner.
Use run_isolated_corpora with immutable CorpusSource pins and native rule selections; retain the default 250-file batch limit.
Compare the five existing Python owners against the same panel plus SARJ560-562, and compare DEFAULT_REGISTRY on the disclosed 30-file panel.
Compare no-test-comments with no-test-comments plus no-frontend-comments using native ESLint with inline configuration disabled.
Run make verify with the pinned tools and a private non-Git temporary root.
